answer: Underwriter liability: a new agent joins only when an established agent writes it a policy, staking copper-grade collateral that pays honest peers if the newcomer is later caught as a clone. Each extra policy one underwriter holds raises its premium along a steep terrace schedule, so a single operator cannot cheaply vouch for a crowd. Since the delta between premium earned and possible loss is thin, underwriters screen hard, and a sybil farm must find many unrelated backers willing to risk real stake.
